claims.claim: Infleqtion's Q2 2026 revenue base is highly concentrated: Customer A represented 82% of Q2 revenue and 74% of first-half revenue; government revenue represented 92% of Q2 and 89% of first-half revenue.

This concentration creates a source-addressed execution risk for Alpha to underwrite: contract timing, appropriations, acceptance milestones or customer-specific changes can materially affect reported growth even when the underlying technology roadmap remains intact.

The risk is concentration and timing sensitivity, not evidence of present deterioration: the same filing reports active commercial and government programs, while contract accounting explicitly depends on progress, acceptance and estimates.

risks.risk: A single customer accounted for 82% of Q2 2026 revenue and government customers accounted for 92%, making quarterly revenue unusually sensitive to a narrow set of contract milestones, budgets and acceptance events.

unknowns.unknown: Alpha still owns the numeric treatment of customer/government concentration and its effect on risk, factor evidence and confidence.

falsifiers: Sustained diversification of revenue across independent commercial customers would materially reduce this concentration risk.
Evidence that Customer A is structurally recurring, multi-program and low-cancellation-risk would reduce the inferred timing sensitivity.
